purpose: Change a panel predicate and trace two formula paths while checking whether they agree on every truth assignment.
meaning: Two propositional formulas are logically equivalent when they have the same truth value for every assignment to their atomic statements. Agreement at the current panel is one row of that comparison. The full four-row table distinguishes a genuine equivalence from a pair that merely happens to match here.

definition.setting: Classical truth-functional equivalence of three fixed pairs of formulas in two independent propositions.

signature.c: Selected formula pair: De Morgan, material implication rewrite or the stated lookalike.

conditions: The panel dimensions x and y independently range from zero to 12 cm. P means x≥6 cm and Q means y≥4 cm, including equality.
All four assignments to P and Q are possible. The complete comparison uses all four, rather than only the selected dimensions.
De Morgan’s pair ¬(P∧Q) and ¬P∨¬Q has zero mismatches. The implication pair P→Q and ¬P∨Q also has zero mismatches.
The lookalike pair ¬(P∧Q) and ¬P∧¬Q differs at the two assignments with exactly one true input. Its other two matching rows do not establish equivalence.
definition.domain_notes: The complete finite truth table establishes equivalence for these propositional truth functions. The distinction is between current assignment truth and agreement for every assignment; it is not a claim about every possible natural-language meaning or arbitrary quantified formula.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Let P mean x≥6 cm and Q mean y≥4 cm. Compare either ¬(P∧Q) with ¬P∨¬Q, P→Q with ¬P∨Q, or the lookalike pair ¬(P∧Q) with ¬P∧¬Q. Evaluate the selected pair on all four truth assignments. Zero mismatches establishes equivalence; the current left and right truth values remain separate from that all-row result.
grammar.precedence: Evaluate P and Q, then inner connectives, then negation. Parentheses keep ¬(P∧Q) distinct from negating each input separately.

properties.claim: De Morgan’s selected formula pair is equivalent.

properties.derivation: If both inputs are true both formulas are false; in the other three cases both formulas are true.

properties.claim: The lookalike pair is not equivalent despite two matching assignments.

prompts.prompt: If the formulas match on this panel, are they equivalent?
prompts.answer: That one row is evidence about the current assignment. Equivalence requires every row to match.
When exactly one of P and Q is true, ¬(P∧Q) is true but ¬P∧¬Q is false.
